messages.content: I get headaches after long days on my laptop. Any tips?

Headaches after long stretches of screen time are common and often linked to eye strain, posture, dehydration or skipped breaks. Many people find the 20-20-20 habit helps: every 20 minutes, look at something about 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Regular water and a short walk can help too.

followUp.question: How long do these headaches usually last?

warningSigns: A sudden, severe headache — the worst you've had
Headache with fever and a stiff neck
Headache with weakness, numbness or trouble speaking

careRecommendation.text: If headaches keep coming back or change in pattern, mention it at your next check-up.

messages.content: How can I build a better sleep routine?

A steady routine is one of the most helpful things for sleep: a similar bedtime and wake time every day, a wind-down period without screens, and a cool, dark room. Your sample data shows you've been sleeping a little longer this month — keeping the same wake-up time on weekends can help that stick.

careRecommendation.text: Worth raising with a clinician if poor sleep lasts several weeks or affects your days.

messages.content: How can I build a better sleep routine?

Your sample data shows you've been sleeping a little longer this month — keeping the same wake-up time on weekends can help that stick.

followUp.question: What usually gets in the way of sleep for you?

careRecommendation.text: Worth raising with a clinician if poor sleep lasts several weeks or affects your days.

memorySuggestions.fact: Gets headaches after long screen sessions

answer.notice: Sample response in Preview mode — not a real AI and not medical advice.
answer.answer: Headaches after long stretches of screen time are common and often linked to eye strain, posture, dehydration or skipped breaks. Many people find the 20-20-20 habit helps: every 20 minutes, look at something about 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Regular water and a short walk can help too.

followUp.question: What usually gets in the way of sleep for you?

careRecommendation.text: Worth raising with a clinician if poor sleep lasts several weeks or affects your days.

answer.notice: Sample response in Preview mode — not a real AI and not medical advice.
answer.answer: A steady routine is one of the most helpful things for sleep: a similar bedtime and wake time every day, a wind-down period without screens, and a cool, dark room. Your sample data shows you've been sleeping a little longer this month — keeping the same wake-up time on weekends can help that stick.
